'''Tan Weihong''' ({{zh|s=谭蔚泓}}; born May 12, 1960) is a Chinese chemist. He is the [[University of Florida]] Distinguished Professor,  V. T. and Louise Jackson Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Florida]],<ref name="Tan Group">{{cite web|title=Weihong Tan|url=https://tan.chem.ufl.edu/|website=University of Florida|publisher=Tan Research Group|accessdate=August 9, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Weihong Tan|url=https://www.chem.ufl.edu/people/name/weihong-tan/|website=University of Florida|publisher=Department of Chemistry|accessdate=August 9, 2016}}</ref> and also the Professor of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Professor of Biology, and Director of the State Key Laboratory of Chemo/Biosensing and Chemometrics at [[Hunan University]] in China.<ref>{{cite web|title=谭蔚泓|url=http://cc.hnu.cn/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=121|website=Hunan University|accessdate=August 9, 2016}}</ref> He was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 2015<ref name=Weihong>{{cite news|title=中国科学院2015年院士增选结果公布|url=http://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2015/12/333401.shtm|website=Kexue Wang|date=December 7, 2015|accessdate=August 9, 2016}}</ref> and [[The World Academy of Sciences]] in 2016.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://english.cas.cn/newsroom/news/201611/t20161117_170678.shtml|title=Nine CAS Scientists Elected TWAS Fellows|date=2016-11-17|publisher=[[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=2019-05-05}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Tan was born on May 12, 1960, in [[Yiyang]], [[Hunan]], China.<ref name=Weihong/> He received his B.S. degree in chemistry from [[Hunan Normal University]] in 1982, his M.S. degree in physical chemistry from the Institute of Coal Chemistry, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1985, and his Ph.D. in physical chemistry from [[University of Michigan, Ann Arbor]] in 1992 under the supervision of Dr. [[Raoul Kopelman]]. In 1994–1995, he conducted his [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Ames Laboratory]] where he worked with Dr. [[Edward Yeung|Edward S. Yeung]].<ref name="Tan Group"/><ref name=Weihong/>

==Research==
The main focus of Tan's group is in the field of DNA [[aptamer]]s, molecular recognition and nano biosensors. The Tan group has pioneered the Whole-Cell [[Systematic Evolution of Ligands by Exponential Enrichment]] method (SELEX). This fundamental tool is used to select [[aptamer]] molecules against specific cell-lines for a wide range of applications. A variety of high sensitive aptamer-based molecular designs have been developed by Tan group and contributed to theranostic and bioanalysis studies.<ref name="Tan Group"/><ref>{{cite book|title=Aptamers Selected by Cell-SELEX for Theranostics|url=https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783662462256|publisher=Springer|accessdate=August 9, 2016}}</ref>

Tan has served on many national and international research program committees, and also several Editorial and Advisory Boards, including [[ACS Nano]] and [[Analytical Chemistry]].

Tan has helped develop a [[COVID-19 testing|test]] for [[COVID-19]] that produced results in as little as 40 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.propublica.org/article/the-trump-administration-drove-him-back-to-china-where-he-invented-a-fast-coronavirus-test|title=The Trump Administration Drove Him Back to China, Where He Invented a Fast Coronavirus Test|last=David Armstrong|first=Annie Waldman|date=2020-03-18|website=ProPublica|language=en|access-date=2020-03-21}}</ref>
